sections.label: Austere prison regime and rehabilitation
sections.summary: Singapore's prison regime is austere with emphasis on security and monitoring, and it focuses on inmate rehabilitation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Our prison regime and prison environment are austere and intentionally so.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We place a lot of emphasis on security and monitoring so that our officers know what is going on.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Our approach is probably one reason, for example, for lower suicide rates in the Singapore prisons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Between 2017 and 2021, there was one case of suicide in Singapore prisons, compared with 10 cases in Hong Kong over the same period, 12 cases in Norway between 2017 and 2020 and 22 cases in Denmark between 2017 and 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We also focus on rehabilitation of our inmates.

sections.label: Cell space size
sections.summary: The cell space is around 10 square metres.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The cell space is around 10 square metres.

sections.label: Mounted fans security risk
sections.summary: Mounted fans could pose a security risk as potential anchor points for suicide.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Mounted fans could pose a security risk because they can be a potential anchor points for suicide.

sections.label: Inmate meals and nutrition
sections.summary: Inmates are given three meals daily, planned based on dieticians' recommendations to meet nutritional requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Next on food and meals, inmates are given three meals daily, planned based on dieticians' recommendations to meet nutritional requirements.

sections.label: Time outside cells for programmes
sections.summary: Inmates in work or programmes may spend two to 10 hours a day outside their cells, depending on programme intensity.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Inmates who work or attend programmes such as psychology-based correctional programmes, family programmes, religious programmes, may spend two to 10 hours a day outside of their cells, depending on the programme intensity.

sections.label: Prison overcrowding and occupancy rates
sections.summary: A 2021 UNODC report states prison overcrowding is widespread, with 47% of 100 countries operating above intended capacity; Singapore is at about 70%.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: A 2021 United Nations Office on Drugs and Crimes (UNODC) report states that prison overcrowding, and I quote, "Prison overcrowding is widespread around the world and of the 100 countries and territories for which UNODC had data on, nearly half, 47%, were operating at more than 100% of the intended capacity." We are at about 70% based on our own standards and assessments.

sections.label: Prison and DRC land area
sections.summary: Land used by prisons and drug rehabilitation centres is about 0.26 square kilometres.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Land area taken up by your prisons and drug rehabilitation centres (DRCs) is about 0.26 square kilometres.

sections.label: Inmate vaccination and mental health
sections.summary: 94% of medically eligible inmates are vaccinated; as of March 2022 about 5% take mental health medication.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Ninety-four percent of medically eligible inmates have been vaccinated against COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Data on inmates diagnosed with mental health conditions upon admission are not actively tracked.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But I can say, as of March 2022, about 5% of inmates are on medication for the management of their mental health conditions.

sections.label: Recidivism rates for release cohorts
sections.summary: The 2019 release cohort recidivism rate is 20%, the lowest in 30 years; the 2015 cohort's five-year rate is 41.7%.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The recidivism rate for the 2019 release cohort is now at 20%, which is the lowest in the last 30 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We can do even better because our five-year recidivism rate for the 2015 release cohort is at 41.7%.

sections.label: Comparison figures for other places
sections.summary: It states comparison figures of 520 for Hong Kong, 270 for England and Wales, 214 for Australia and 105 for South Korea.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In comparison, 520 for Hong Kong, 270 for England and Wales, 214 for Australia and 105 for South Korea.

sections.label: Prisons run by officers
sections.summary: Prisons officers run prisons fairly and with discipline, with zero tolerance for gang activities and disciplinary actions including corporal punishment.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Our Prisons officers run our prisons – not inmates, not gangs.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Prisons are run in a fair and disciplined manner.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We have a zero-tolerance stance towards gang-related activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Prisons takes disciplinary actions against those found to be involved in such activities, including corporal punishments – Prisons can mete out.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The point is we maintain more control and on the whole, less of these bad things happen compared with most other places.

sections.label: Follow-up care for ex-offenders
sections.summary: Inmates with conditions may be referred to IMH or restructured hospitals, and ex-offenders needing follow-up go to Changi General Hospital clinics.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Prior to release, inmates with mental and medical conditions may be referred to IMH or restructured hospitals for follow-up care.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Ex-offenders who need further follow-up after release are referred to Changi General Hospital's specialist clinics for continuity of care.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Prisons is working with SingHealth to facilitate follow-up appointments for ex-offenders at other public healthcare institutions which are nearer to their home.

sections.label: Alternative bedding materials search
sections.summary: MHA has looked at possible alternative bedding materials but has not found a possible substitute.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In this regard, is MHA looking into actively any other materials that can be used as an alternative to the current bedding that is being used right now?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We have been looking at possible alternative materials for some time and I do not think we have come across anything that we have seen as a possible substitute that can be used.

sections.label: COVID-19 in prisons
sections.summary: Prisons require care due to proximity and time spent together, and 94% of eligible inmates had been vaccinated.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On COVID-19, Prisons is obviously a place where we need to be careful because of the proximity and the amount of time people spend with each other.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I do not have the data here but I gave you earlier that 94% of eligible inmates had been vaccinated.

sections.label: Prison assault rates
sections.summary: Prisons generally do not publish assault rates, but the understanding is Singapore prison assault rates are much lower.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Data is not easy to get because it is not as if prisons, generally, publish the assault rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But my own understanding is that the assault rates in Singapore prisons are, generally, much lower.

sections.label: Censored newspapers in prisons
sections.summary: Newspapers are made available after content such as reports on rapes, assaults and violence is removed.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The newspapers would be made available after the prisons have gone through the newspapers, the contents, and they have removed some content.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: For example, reports on rapes, assaults, violence, those sorts of things are taken out because when people read it, there is a sense that they might then be inclined to engage in such conduct.

sections.label: Live television not allowed
sections.summary: Live television programmes are not allowed because they cannot be censored before being put out.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Likewise, live television programmes are not allowed for the same reason, because you cannot censor and then put it out.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I am looking for the data in my earlier speech, going back to Mr Murali Pillai's question.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I did give the data on assault rates.
